the stiffness of the major arteries increases with advancing age and the stiffness indices calculated by this method can be used to evaluate the mechanical properties of major human arteries in vivo.
the stiffness of major arteries increases significantly with age, but the age associated changes in the mechanical properties of major arteries are less pronounced than those of the smaller arteries.
the age associated increase in the stiffness index is statistically significant only in central elastic arteries and is less pronounced in the peripheral muscular arteries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of an ultrasonic method for non-invasive assessment of arterial stiffness.
the age-related changes in the mechanical properties of large elastic and muscular arteries in the human.
the development of a new method for the non-invasive assessment of age related changes in the stiffness of the major branches of the arteries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the age-related change of arterial stiffness is a continuous process and the stiffness of the major arteries increases significantly with advancing age.
, with advancing age, the diameter of all major arteries increases and the percentage change in diameter with a change in blood pressure decreases.
the age associated increase in arterial stiffness is a generalized phenomenon, which is more marked in the central arteries, and is not influenced significantly by vasoactive factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the stiffness indices calculated for the central arteries provide a reliable measure of the mechanical properties of these vessels, and that the peripheral arteries are influenced by the measuring conditions.
the stiffness indices calculated from the ultrasonic measurements of the diameter and pressure are a reliable and non-invasive method for assessing the mechanical properties of major arteries.
the age related changes are more pronounced in the central arteries and that the peripheral arteries show considerable variation in the degree and direction of the changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are significant differences in the age related changes between different arteries, and that the peripheral arteries are more vulnerable to environmental influences than the central arteries.
the stiffness indices calculated from the diameter-pressure relationship of the brachial artery are not a reliable indicator of age-related changes in arterial stiffness.
